m6-t1.question: Why is eight of ten closed tasks not necessarily 80% complete?
options: Every task must have identical dates
Tasks may represent different effort or value
m6-t1.explanation: Progress requires a defined basis, not automatic equal weighting.

m6-t1.question: What should RAG thresholds be?
options: Agreed before applying them to the report
Changed to keep every project green

m6-t1.question: What date belongs beside a baseline milestone?
options: The current forecast and any actual date
m6-t1.explanation: Comparing baseline and forecast reveals variance.

m6-t1.question: Which decision request is actionable?
options: Approve or defer the reminder change by Thursday
m6-t1.explanation: A clear choice and deadline support action.

m6-t1.question: A critical unresolved security defect exists. What should the report do?
options: Count it as a minor completed task
Show it explicitly even if other dimensions are green

m6-t2.question: What is the difference between a position and an interest?
options: An interest is only a financial rate
A position is the demand; an interest is the underlying need
They always mean the same thing
m6-t2.explanation: Understanding needs can reveal alternative solutions.

m6-t2.question: The required approver is absent. How should the result be labelled?
m6-t2.explanation: Authority cannot be manufactured by the minutes.

m6-t2.question: What is essential in decision minutes?
options: Decision, authority, rationale and follow-up ownership
m6-t2.explanation: The record must explain what happens next and why.

m6-t2.question: Which concession is not appropriate?
options: Removing mandatory safety checks to meet the date
Deferring an optional feature after approval
m6-t2.explanation: Mandatory controls are not casual bargaining chips.

m6-t2.question: What should happen to an unresolved vendor concern?
options: Call it resolved because the meeting ended
Replace it with a success statement
Record it as an open action with an owner
Remove it to simplify the minutes

m6-t3.question: What primarily distinguishes a portfolio?
options: Every project must use the same software
All work has one identical deadline
It is only a list of completed tasks
Investments are selected and balanced for strategic objectives
m6-t3.explanation: Portfolio management considers strategic alignment and resources.

m6-t3.question: What is A’s score at equal weights for scores 4 and 2?
Why test scoring-weight sensitivity?
options: To see whether the recommendation is fragile
m6-t3.explanation: A ranking that reverses easily needs careful interpretation.

m6-t3.question: Who should own a continuing benefit after handover?
options: A named operational role with authority to measure it
No one once the project closes
m6-t3.explanation: Benefits outlive the temporary delivery team.

m6-t3.question: What should a PMO analyst confirm before approving expenditure?
options: Whether the project name sounds urgent
Whether their role has that authority
m6-t3.explanation: Reporting responsibility does not automatically grant approval authority.

questions.question: A report shows baseline launch Friday and forecast Tuesday after it. What should not be done?
options: Replace the baseline date silently to erase variance
questions.explanation: Silently overwriting the reference destroys control history.

questions.question: Equal-weight scores are A: 5 and 1, B: 3 and 4. Which ranks higher on that model?
options: A because its first score is 5
questions.explanation: Weighted averages are 3.0 and 3.5; constraints still matter.

questions.question: The portfolio ranking reverses when a weight changes modestly. What should the analyst communicate?
options: Sensitivity and the need to inspect assumptions
The first ranking is objective truth
No decision can ever be made

questions.question: A meeting ends with broad support but no authorised approver present. How should minutes describe the choice?
questions.explanation: Support does not substitute for required authority.

questions.question: A project is green on cost but red on a critical unresolved dependency. What should the summary do?
options: Hide the dependency in an appendix only
Use cost alone to decide status
Show the critical dependency explicitly, not average it away
questions.explanation: Dimensions and critical exceptions require transparent reporting.

questions.question: Two initiatives claim the same eight staff-hours saved per event. What should PMO check?
options: Only the sum of both claims
questions.explanation: Portfolio benefits should not count the same effect twice.

questions.question: An analyst has reporting responsibility but no spending authority. What is the appropriate output?
questions.explanation: Responsibility for analysis does not confer approval authority.

questions.question: A sponsor needs a choice by Thursday; the report contains twenty pages of tasks. What revision is most useful?
options: Put the decision, options and deadline in the opening summary
questions.explanation: The brief should reduce decision effort while preserving traceability.

questions.question: Minutes record “vendor will improve” without owner or date. What is missing?
options: A concrete action, responsible role and due date

questions.question: A project closes before the benefit measurement window. What should the benefits register include?
options: A claim of full benefit at closure
An accepting operations owner and scheduled review
questions.explanation: Post-project benefits need continuing ownership and measurement.
